newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: West Africans seek business at U.S. building show.
newsitem.headline: West Africans seek business at U.S. building show.

text.p: A group of 70 business leaders from 15 West African states leaves Abidjan on Tuesday to seek joint ventures at a four-day home builders show in Houston, Texas, the U.S. Commercial Service said.
"The general purpose of the visit is to promote trade and investment between American builders and the growing construction sector in West Africa," said a U.S. Commercial Service statement.

The business executives will attend the January 24-27 National Association of Home Builders Show featuring more than 2,000 major exhibitors displaying items ranging from carpeting to design, insulation and entertainment systems.

On the way to Houston, the Africans stop in Brussels for meetings with representatives of 14 state business development offices to discuss opportunities in the individual U.S. states, a Commercial Service statement said.

Business analysts said the trip, coming less than a week after the visit of a large U.S. business mission to West Africa, underlined a concerted U.S. bid to challenge French business dominance in the region.
The group from both Francophone and English-speaking states is led jointly by the U.S. ambassador to Ivory Coast, Lannon Walker, and his counterpart in Ghana, Edward Brynn.
